marks.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבא: ואימא מדרבנן -- גורר את הטפילה עד שיהא בארץ [-- that would support Reish Lakish]; אלא אמר רבא: הכי קאמר ... (= p_rava_hachi_kaamar_tanur)
אמר מר: חולקו לשלשה. ורמינהו: ... the Sages: of a large one [remains of four]; טעמא דאיכא שייריו ארבע, הא ליכא שייריו ארבע -- טהור [even without dividing in three]
R' Meir: an oven -- its start is four [handbreadths], and its remains four
אמרי: התם דצלקיה מצלק, הכא דעבדיה גיסטרא -- there he cut it horizontally; here he made it a shard
אמר מר: שייריו ברובו -- רובו דטפח למאי הוי? -- [if 'any size' is a handbreadth,] what use is the majority of a handbreadth?
אמר אביי: שיירי גדול ברובו (= p_abaye_shirei_gadol_berubo)
והאמרי רבנן ארבעה? -- but the Rabbis said [the large oven's remains are] four!
לא קשיא: הא בתנורא בר תשעה, הא בתנורא בר שבעה -- one of a nine-handbreadth oven, the other of a seven
Abaye: [the clause means] the remains of a large one in its majority
איתיביה: ... כי ממעט מיהא טהור, אמאי? לימא חשיב!
הכא במאי עסקינן -- דקא בעי ליה למושב זב: here he wants it for a zav's seat (no speaker marked; Steinsaltz gives it to Reish Lakish)
R' Meir: he need neither scrape the plaster nor [take it] to the ground; rather he reduces it from within below four handbreadths

Rava: this is what [the mishna] says -- an impure oven: all agree one divides it into three and scrapes the plaster to the ground; one who wants his oven never to become impure -- [the first tanna:] divides and scrapes; R' Meir: reduces it from within below four
the Sages: when is this said? of a large [oven]
the school of R' Yannai: 'any size' is a handbreadth, for they make girls' ovens of a handbreadth
R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei: and even if he left a scarf's measure [it is not joined]
Reish Lakish: they taught this only of a garment; but [the scarf's measure left in] a hide is significant
a hide on which there is an olive-bulk of flesh: one who touches a strand coming out of it, or a hair opposite it, is impure
if there were on it [the like of] two half-olive-bulks -- it imparts impurity by carrying
כדאמר רב פפא -- the stam applies Rav Pappa's במרודד (said of R' Yishmael's clause, 124b.21) to R' Yochanan's dictum
ואלא קשיא? -- if Ravin's [reisha] version stands, the difficulty Rav Nachman and R' Ami raised (even a tarta, even a sifter) remains
R' Yochanan [per Ulla]: they taught [that the olive-bulk on the hide imparts impurity] only where an animal severed it
even [flesh the size of] a tarta? -- yes
because Rav Nachman is the son-in-law of the Nasi's house, he belittles R' Yochanan's teaching?!
R' Yochanan [per R' Ami, on the seifa -- two half-olives]: they taught it only where an animal severed it
